name: Security Rulebook
summary: Protecting visitors, data, money and the budget: from headers to authentication, access control, prices and paid APIs. Attack library and checklist: security/.
check: Run `node scripts/proui-security-scan.mjs . --build <build dir>` and fix every hard finding.
Go through security/CHECKLIST.md at the right level and run the self-tests in security/PROBES.md against localhost or staging.
`curl -I` the live site for headers; `npm audit`.

rules.title: HTTPS only
rules.text: The site is served only over HTTPS, with HSTS (`Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`) once HTTPS is confirmed working.

rules.title: Content Security Policy
rules.text: A CSP header (or meta tag on static hosting) that allows only the origins the site really uses; no `unsafe-eval`, avoid `unsafe-inline` for scripts (use nonces or hashes).

rules.title: Security headers
rules.text: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Permissions-Policy` that turns off unused features (camera, microphone, geolocation), and `frame-ancestors 'none'` (or `X-Frame-Options: DENY`) unless embedding is wanted.

rules.title: Secrets in the client
rules.text: API keys with write access, tokens and passwords never appear in front-end code, the repository or build output. Use environment variables on the server; commit an `.env.example`, never `.env`.

rules.title: Validate input on the server
rules.text: Every form and API endpoint checks type, length and format on the server, not only in the browser.

rules.title: Escape output
rules.text: Never insert user content as HTML (`innerHTML`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `v-html`) without sanitising it; prefer text nodes.

rules.title: Injection-safe data access
rules.text: Parameterised queries or an ORM; no string-built SQL; the database user has only the rights it needs.

rules.title: Forms protected from abuse
rules.text: CSRF protection on state-changing requests, rate limiting, and spam protection that does not punish people (honeypot field, time check, or a privacy-friendly challenge).

rules.title: Safe cookies and sessions
rules.text: `Secure`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax` (or `Strict`) cookies; sessions expire; log-out really ends the session.

rules.title: Authentication done properly
rules.text: When the site has accounts: use a proven provider or library, hash passwords with a slow algorithm (argon2 or bcrypt), offer two-factor where it matters, and never reveal whether an email is registered.

rules.title: Safe uploads
rules.text: When the site accepts files: check type and size on the server, rename files, store them outside the web root or in object storage, and never execute them.

rules.title: Restricted CORS
rules.text: Allow only the origins that need the API; never `*` with credentials.

rules.title: Third-party code is pinned and checked
rules.text: Exact versions for CDN scripts with Subresource Integrity (`integrity` + `crossorigin`), sandboxed iframes for embeds, as few third-party scripts as possible.

rules.title: Dependencies audited
rules.text: Run `npm audit` (or the stack's equivalent) and fix high and critical issues; remove unused packages (`PF-07`); keep a lockfile.

rules.title: Errors without leaks
rules.text: Production error pages and API errors show a friendly message, never stack traces, file paths, queries or versions.

rules.title: Safe external links
rules.text: `rel="noopener noreferrer"` on links that open in a new tab.

rules.title: Collect only what is needed
rules.text: Minimal personal data, stored securely, with a retention period and a way to delete it; matches the privacy policy (`PE-08`).

rules.title: Security contact
rules.text: `/.well-known/security.txt` with a contact address for reporting issues.

rules.title: Rate-limit sign-in and forms
rules.text: Repeated failed sign-ins, password resets and form posts are slowed down or blocked per IP and account.

rules.title: Verify webhooks
rules.text: Incoming webhooks (payments, forms) are checked by signature before anything happens.

rules.title: Least-privilege keys
rules.text: API keys and service accounts have only the rights they need, and are rotated when people leave or keys leak.

rules.title: Expiring reset links
rules.text: Password reset and magic links are single-use and expire within about an hour.

rules.title: Storing card data
rules.text: Never store or log card numbers. Use the payment provider's hosted fields or checkout.

rules.title: Exposed internals on the server
rules.text: No reachable `.git`, `.env`, backups, directory listings or server version headers in production.

rules.title: Your own crypto
rules.text: Never invent hashing, encryption or token schemes. Use the platform's and well-known libraries' implementations.

rules.title: Personal data in logs and URLs
rules.text: Logs, analytics and URLs never contain passwords, tokens, card data or unnecessary personal data.

rules.title: Check the owner on every object
rules.text: Every read, change or download of a private object (order, invoice, file, message, profile) is filtered by the signed-in user on the server: `where: { id, userId: session.user.id }`, answering 404 otherwise. Changing the ID in the URL must never show someone else's data. Add row-level security in the database as a second wall where it exists (`security/attacks/access-control.md`, AT-10).

rules.title: Admin routes checked on the server
rules.text: Every admin page and every admin API route checks the role on the server, from the session or the database, inside the handler as well as in middleware. A hidden link, an unlisted URL or a client-side check is not protection. Staff accounts use two-factor sign-in (AT-11).

rules.title: Allow-list the fields a request may set
rules.text: Never save a request body as it came (`create({ data: req.body })`). Parse it with a schema that lists the allowed fields, so `role`, `isAdmin`, `credits`, `price` or `verified` sent by an attacker are dropped (AT-12).

rules.title: The server sets every price
rules.text: The browser sends what the person wants (product, variant, quantity, coupon code); the server looks up prices, discounts, shipping and tax and computes the total, and creates the payment amount itself. Quantities are whole numbers from 1 to a sensible maximum; totals never go below zero (AT-30, AT-31).

rules.title: One-time things are used atomically
rules.text: Coupons, gift-card balances, referral bonuses, the last item in stock and one-time codes are checked and used in one atomic step (a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL RETURNING`, a unique constraint or a locking transaction). Money-moving requests carry an idempotency key, so a double click or a replay creates one order (AT-33, AT-34).

rules.title: Budgets and limits on every paid API
rules.text: Every paid service (AI, maps, search, SMS, voice, storage egress) has a hard budget with alerts at the provider, per-user and per-IP rate limits, and limits fixed on the server: the model, the maximum output tokens, the number of tool calls, the voice minutes. Expensive calls need sign-in; repeated results are cached; images are resized once and served from a CDN with hotlinking blocked (AT-70, AT-83).

rules.title: AI features that trust the prompt
rules.text: Never treat a system prompt as a security boundary or let a model's answer grant anything. Put no secrets in prompts; give tools the least power (read-only, one user's data); confirm side effects with the user; render model output as sanitised text so it cannot load outside images or run scripts; build each user's context only from their own data (AT-80 to AT-82).

rules.title: Secrets in Git, now or ever
rules.text: `.env*` files are ignored before the first commit, with a `.env.example` of names only; a secret scan runs before commits and in CI. A key that was ever pushed is rotated at the provider first, then removed from the history, because it must be assumed copied (AT-61).

rules.title: Server-side fetches only to allowed hosts
rules.text: A feature that fetches a URL given by a user (link previews, imports, webhooks to test) fetches only allow-listed hosts, refuses private, loopback and link-local addresses after resolving and after redirects, and has short timeouts and size limits (AT-52).

rules.title: Redirect only to your own paths
rules.text: `next`, `returnTo` and `callbackUrl` parameters accept only relative paths on the same site (starting with `/`, not `//`), checked against an allow-list; OAuth redirect URIs are registered exactly (AT-42, AT-25).

rules.title: File paths and shell commands from input
rules.text: Never build a file path, an archive entry path or a shell command from user input. Map IDs to stored paths, check that resolved paths stay inside their folder, and call programs with `execFile` and an argument array (AT-04, AT-51).
